summary: This article explains how pearl divers of the Arabian Gulf, including the eastern coast of Saudi Arabia, worked the sea for pearls and why the trade came to an end.
introduce: Write First, Next, Then, and Finally on the board and ask a volunteer to use them to describe how they get ready for school. Tell students to watch for the order of events as they read “Pearl Divers of the Gulf”.

keyTerms.def: a traditional wooden sailing boat used in the Gulf and Indian Ocean
a group of people who work together, especially on a ship
one flat level of something lying on top of another

challengeTerms.def: something that bothers or rubs against a body part
the smooth, shiny material that lines the inside of some shells; also called mother-of-pearl
grown by people on purpose, not formed only by nature

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that pearl divers had one of the hardest jobs in history? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two reasons pearl diving declined in the Gulf and how this changed people's lives.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review dhow, crew, and layer, and let weak readers put sentence strips of the main events in order before writing.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses irritant, nacre, and cultured to summarize the key events in order and explain which step matters most.
